lessons.title: Hand tools and how to use them
lessons.html:
The right tool for the job

Using the wrong tool damages parts, breaks tools and causes injuries. A good mechanic chooses the right tool, uses it correctly and looks after it.

Spanners and sockets

  • Ring spanner: grips all six corners of a nut. Use it for tight nuts.
  • Open-end spanner: quick to use but can slip on tight nuts.
  • Combination spanner: ring on one end, open on the other.
  • Socket and ratchet: fast work. Six-point sockets grip better than twelve-point.
  • Impact sockets: thick black sockets for impact wrenches. Never use normal chrome sockets on an impact wrench; they can shatter.

Always pull a spanner towards you rather than pushing, so your hand does not hit something if it slips. Never put a pipe on a spanner to make it longer.

Other hand tools

ToolCorrect useNever
ScrewdriversMatch tip to screw headUse as a chisel or pry bar
PliersGripping, bending, cutting wireUse on nuts
HammersBall pein for metal, soft-face for finished partsUse with a loose head
Chisels and punchesCutting and driving pinsUse with a mushroomed head
FilesSmoothing metal, always with a handleUse without a handle
PullersRemoving bearings and gearsUse without safety glasses

Torque wrench

A torque wrench tightens bolts to the exact value in the manual. Set it, pull smoothly until it clicks, then stop. Set it back to the lowest setting after use and never use it to undo bolts.

Looking after tools

Clean tools after use. Put them back in the toolbox or shadow board. Report broken tools and do not use them.

lessons.title: Power tools and workshop equipment
lessons.html:
Power tools

Power tools save time but can cause serious injury. Check each tool before use: cable and plug not damaged, guards in place, switch working.

  • Electric drill: clamp the work, use sharp bits, wear glasses. No gloves near the turning chuck.
  • Angle grinder: keep the guard on, use the right disc for the job and speed, wear a face shield and gloves, hold with both hands. Never use a cutting disc for grinding. Point sparks away from fuel and people.
  • Impact wrench (electric or air): use impact sockets only. Do not use it to tighten wheel nuts or critical bolts to final torque; finish with a torque wrench.
  • Air tools: check hoses and couplings. Never point compressed air at yourself or anyone else; it can enter the skin or eyes.

Workshop equipment

EquipmentSafe use
Hydraulic jackLift only on the correct jacking points, then support on stands
Axle standsRated for the load, on firm level ground
Overhead crane or engine hoistCheck rated load, use a checked sling, never stand under
Bench viceUse soft jaws for finished parts; do not hammer on the handle
Bench grinderTool rest close to the wheel, eye shield down, stand to the side when starting
Hydraulic pressGuard in place, part well supported, wear a face shield
Parts washerUse approved solvent, gloves and glasses, no flames nearby

Lifting equipment

Cranes, hoists, slings and chains must be inspected regularly and marked with their safe working load. Do not use lifting gear that is damaged or not marked. Ask your supervisor if you are not trained on a piece of equipment.

Electrical tools outdoors

On farms, you may work far from the workshop. Use a generator or extension lead with an earth leakage unit. Keep leads out of water and mud.

Key points

  • Choose the right tool and check it before use.
  • Pull spanners towards you and never extend them with a pipe.
  • Use impact sockets only on impact wrenches.
  • Keep grinder guards on and wear a face shield.
  • Support lifted tractors on stands and never stand under a load.
